<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Models and meaning</p><h1>What’s Artificial Intelligence all about?</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>14 Feb 2025</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>One way to demystify a model is to build a tiny one. A small automatic-differentiation engine makes the chain rule, gradients, and parameter updates concrete.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>What is the smallest useful object that lets us watch a model learn?</p><h2>The construction</h2><p>Values carry parents and local derivatives. A backward pass applies the chain rule through the graph. The implementation is intentionally small enough that every operation can be read.</p><pre><code>loss.backward()
for parameter in parameters:
    parameter.value += -step * parameter.grad</code></pre><p>The point is not to recreate a production framework. It is to turn a black box into a box with transparent walls.</p></article></main>
